"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Meeting the threat from terrorism and international crime requires new measures and consistent policies and determination from America's leaders.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Many established terrorist groups faded away in the 1990s after the Cold War ended.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Terrorists are increasingly motivated by amorphous religious causes or simple hatred of America rather than by specific political aims.",
"claim_types":["characterization"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Terrorism crosses borders easily and frequently, including U.S. borders, and cannot easily be categorized as either domestic or international.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Support for a response to terrorism that is resolute but not impulsive.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"The most likely highly destructive terrorist attack remains a large bomb hidden in a car or truck.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"The United States must be extremely vigilant about the possibility that future terrorists might use weapons of mass destruction, which are increasingly available and present an unprecedented threat to America.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"The military will have to rethink its traditional doctrine and begin to focus on counterterrorism, human intelligence gathering, and unconventional warfare.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"Weapons of mass destruction are increasingly available.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[4]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
